daily_brief: World leaders convened in New York on Tuesday for the UN General Assembly's annual high-level debate, with some 130 heads of state expected to address conflicts in Iran, Ukraine, Sudan, and Yemen, alongside concerns over AI governance and climate change [RFI]. Presidents Macron and Trump held what the French leader described as 'very constructive' talks on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and pursuing an 'energy truce' between Russia and Ukraine amid surging oil prices [RFI, France 24]. The G7 foreign ministers issued a joint statement demanding Iran cease arming the Houthis in Yemen, warning that recent escalation threatens regional and global energy security [BBC]. Major US television networks suspended pooled coverage of the White House after CNN, Politico and MS NOW were barred, prompting the administration to launch its own streaming channel, Trump TV [BBC]. A joint investigation by RFI and 23 media outlets revealed the US has deported over 25,000 people to third countries since Trump's return to power, with some sent to African nations where they face detention without legal status [RFI, The Guardian]. In Turkey, an 11-person shooting outside a high school in Manisa marked the country's third such incident this year [BBC, Al Jazeera].

top_stories.headline: UN General Assembly Opens Amid Multiple Crises as World Leaders Seek Diplomatic Progress
bullets: Approximately 130 heads of state and government are gathering in New York for the UN General Assembly's annual high-level debate
Key agenda items include conflicts in Iran, Gaza, Ukraine, Sudan, DRC and Myanmar, as well as climate change, economic pressures and AI governance concerns
UN Secretary-General António Guterres will deliver his final address before his term ends December 31, with no clear successor yet emerged
The 193 member states have agreed to a broad reform package including efforts to update the Security Council structure

sources.name: RFI English
sources.framing_note: Emphasized the breadth of challenges and institutional questions facing the UN

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Focused on leadership transitions and speculation about Guterres' successor

top_stories.headline: Macron and Trump Discuss Reopening Strait of Hormuz and Ukraine Energy Truce
bullets: French President Macron met with President Trump in New York ahead of the UN General Assembly, describing talks as 'very constructive'
Macron proposed measures to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which has been disrupted since the outbreak of war involving Iran, Israel and the US in February
Paris seeks a UN Security Council resolution guaranteeing freedom of navigation through the strait, which normally carries 20% of global oil and gas trade
The leaders also discussed protecting Saudi oil infrastructure and pursuing an 'energy truce' between Russia and Ukraine

sources.name: RFI English
sources.framing_note: Detailed French diplomatic proposals and energy market concerns

sources.framing_note: Focused on the bilateral meeting dynamics

top_stories.headline: G7 Demands Iran Stop Arming Houthis as Yemen Conflict Escalates
bullets: G7 foreign ministers issued a joint statement calling on Iran to 'end its arming of and support' for the Houthis in Yemen
The statement condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and warned the escalation threatens regional and global energy security
Thousands of refugees have fled Yemen after Houthis seized territory along the Red Sea coastline, including near the Bab al-Mandab Strait
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced Britain will provide air-to-air refuelling support to Saudi Arabia for a matter of weeks

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Emphasized G7 diplomatic pressure and regional security concerns

sources.name: The Hindu

top_stories.headline: Major US Networks Suspend Pooled White House Coverage After Media Ban
bullets: Major US television networks suspended pooled coverage of President Trump after CNN, Politico and MS NOW were barred from the White House on Friday
The three banned outlets announced they will sue the Trump administration to 'defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports'
The White House launched Trump TV, a 24/7 streaming channel featuring clips of the president
New York Times and Washington Post declined to share still images from Trump events; no network footage aired of Trump boarding Air Force One or arriving in New York

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Reported factually on the boycott and lawsuit announcement

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Referenced 'great deal of scepticism' about the new channel

top_stories.headline: Investigation Reveals US Deporting Migrants to Third Countries Across Africa
bullets: More than 25,000 people have been deported from the US to third countries since Trump's return to power, according to a six-month investigation by 24 media outlets
At least 12 African countries have agreed to receive deportees, including Central African Republic and Equatorial Guinea
Some deportees were sent to countries they have no connection to; others were later sent to places where they risked persecution or torture
Witnesses reported deportees in Equatorial Guinea were bound, beaten, and detained in a hotel where about 30 remain trapped

sources.name: RFI English
sources.framing_note: Part of coordinated 'Deportation Project' investigation; focused on individual stories and systematic process

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.framing_note: Emphasized human rights concerns and detailed accounts of abuse in detention
